title: Feasibility of Establishing Body to Regulate Artificial Intelligence
what_it_is: Feasibility of Establishing Body to Regulate Artificial Intelligence

sections.label: Singapore supports responsible AI development
sections.summary: Singapore supports responsible development and deployment of AI to unlock its potential for the economy and society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Singapore supports the responsible development and deployment of artificial intelligence (AI) to unlock its transformative potential on our economy and society.

sections.label: Model AI Governance Framework
sections.summary: In 2019, PDPC published the Model AI Governance Framework to turn AI ethical principles into implementable business practices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In 2019, PDPC published the Model AI Governance Framework to turn AI ethical principles into implementable business practices for companies to safely deploy AI solutions.

sections.label: Advisory Guidelines on AI personal data
sections.summary: PDPC will issue Advisory Guidelines on the Use of Personal Data in AI Systems later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Later this year, PDPC will be issuing Advisory Guidelines on the Use of Personal Data in AI Systems to provide guidance on how the Personal Data Protection Act will apply to the collection and use of personal data in AI systems for decision-making, predictions or recommendations.

sections.label: ASEAN Guide on AI Governance
sections.summary: As upcoming ADGMIN Chair, Singapore hopes to work with ASEAN member states on an ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: As the upcoming Chair of the Fourth ASEAN Digital Ministers Meeting (ADGMIN), Singapore hopes to work with fellow ASEAN member states to develop an ASEAN Guide on AI Governance and Ethics.

sections.label: AI regulation measures and standards
sections.summary: AI regulatory measures like seat belts and traffic lights must be built up, with international standards and frameworks emerging.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, my own sense of it is that, in AI, the equivalent of the seat belts, the air bags, the equivalent of the traffic lights, the speed limits, all these things will have to be built up.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: And back to the Member's question then about whether there will be a central agency that can be effective in regulating AI, it remains to be seen because we have to understand what the useful regulatory measures are in the first place.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: All of these regulations have to inter-operate with our counterparts overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, international standards, what will be useful, these things will be developed.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We will see the emergence of new standards, new certifications and new regulatory frameworks.

sections.label: Singapore's advantage moving fast
sections.summary: When it is clearer what is necessary and useful, Singapore's advantage is moving fast and sustaining it.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: When it has become clearer what is necessary and useful, I think Singapore's advantage is in being able to move quite fast and that is the advantage that we should try and sustain over time.
